A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the best PFS for perfusion media are those with no halogen atoms and which are not firmly linked to tissue.
a straight chain perfluoroalkane with a vapor pressure of 0.5 mm Hg or less, and which contains iodine or bromide atoms, should be the most useful PFS for clinical use.
the best oxygen solvents for organ perfusion are perfluorocarbons with no terminal halogen atoms, which can be emulsified with Pluronic F-68 and Vitrum phospholipids.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the most useful emulsions are made from perfluorocarbons that leave the liver, and that the emulsifier is the most important factor in determining the toxicity and biocompatibility of a perfluorocarbonate emulsion.
the best emulsion for perfusion is a 10% perfluoromethyldecain in 1.5% Pluronic F-68 emulsion.
the most promising PFS are those which are nontoxically excreted from the body and which do not produce morphological changes in the liver.
